original_question: Let X be a Banach lattice for which there exists a weakly compact set L ⊆ X whose generated sublattice is dense in X. Must X be weakly compactly generated, that is, must there exist a weakly compact set K ⊆ X with X = span(K)?
target_in_paper: Problem 1.4 (Diestel) in Section 1.2 of arXiv:1607.07787, with the precise Banach-lattice formulation formalized in the cited companion paper [6] as the question whether every LWCG Banach lattice is WCG.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the intended problem almost verbatim: the ambient object is a Banach lattice X, the hypothesis is the existence of a weakly compact set whose generated sublattice is dense in X, and the conclusion asked for is exactly the WCG property, expressed as existence of a weakly compact linear generator.
missing_details: The paper works over real Banach spaces, so X should be a real Banach lattice.
It is best to say explicitly that WCG means: there exists a weakly compact set K whose closed linear span is X.

To avoid ambiguity, 'the sublattice generated by L' should be phrased as the smallest sublattice of X containing L; in the companion paper [6], sublattices are taken to be closed, so this becomes X = L(L), i.e. X is LWCG.
The density involved is norm density in X, while weak compactness is with respect to the Banach-space weak topology.

No extra assumptions such as order continuity, Dedekind completeness, separability, or weak sequential continuity should be added; the paper treats some of those as special cases where the answer is already known.
refined_question: Let X be a real Banach lattice. Suppose there exists a weakly compact set L contained in X such that the smallest sublattice of X containing L is norm dense in X. Must there exist a weakly compact set K contained in X whose closed linear span is all of X?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if a real Banach lattice X is weakly compactly generated as a lattice (LWCG), meaning that X = L(K) for some weakly compact set K and L(K) denotes the smallest closed sublattice of X containing K, must X be weakly compactly generated (WCG)?
justification: The draft is targeting the survey's Problem 1.4 exactly: Section 1.2 first recalls the definition of WCG and then states Diestel's question in essentially the same words. The nearby context also says that the order-continuous case was already proved in the affirmative by the cited paper [6]. In that companion paper, Section 1 makes the formulation precise by introducing LWCG in Definition 1.1(i), and later results explain the intended scope: Theorem 3.1 settles the order-continuous case, while Theorem 4.3 shows the general LWCG-versus-WCG problem can be reduced to Banach lattices with order continuous dual. So the sharp stand-alone reformulation is the general LWCG implies WCG question, with only the implicit conventions (real scalars, norm density, and closed linear span) made explicit.
